page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128g-960s is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. However, multi-core performance, such as stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations also register in the average tier, though the overall PassMark memory score remains strong. For lightweight AI workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models, but drops to average performance when processing medium 7B models.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound workloads without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware. The combination of dedicated compute resources, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 960 GB of NVMe storage makes it appropriate for database operations, text processing, memory-intensive web serving, and software compilation tasks that do not require massive multi-threaded parallelization.
